10 Which quantities are conserved in an inelastic collision?
kinetic energy
total energy
linear momentum
A
conserved
not conserved
conserved
B
conserved
not conserved
not conserved
C
not conserved
conserved
conserved
D
not conserved
conserved
not conserved

hints: Notice the word inelastic in the stem - it is defined by what happens to kinetic energy compared with an elastic collision.
Recall that total energy can never disappear but kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ can be changed into heat and sound during impact.
Check linear momentum separately: with no external resultant force the vector sum $mv$ before equals the vector sum after, even if kinetic energy is lost.
walkthrough: Identify the three quantities in the table: kinetic energy, total energy and linear momentum for an inelastic collision.
State the definition: an inelastic collision is one in which the total kinetic energy after is less than before because some is transferred to thermal energy, sound and permanent deformation.
Apply conservation of energy: energy cannot be created or destroyed, so the lost kinetic energy still exists in other forms and total energy is conserved.

Apply conservation of momentum: provided there is no external resultant force, Newton's laws give $m_1u_1 + m_2u_2 = m_1v_1 + m_2v_2$, so linear momentum is conserved in both elastic and inelastic collisions.
Combine the results as not conserved, conserved, conserved. This is option C

A.explanation: Kinetic energy is not conserved in an inelastic collision, so claiming it is conserved is wrong.

B.explanation: Both claims are wrong because kinetic energy is lost and linear momentum is still conserved in an inelastic collision.

C.explanation: Kinetic energy is not conserved but is transferred to other forms, so total energy and linear momentum remain conserved.

D.explanation: Linear momentum is conserved when no external resultant force acts, so claiming it is not conserved is wrong.
